gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's per-chip count behind the 'base M1/M2/M3' warning: M1 and M2 MacBook Airs drive one external display, the M3's two-display mode works only with the lid closed (the second display goes dark when the lid opens, so it cannot serve a screen hung on an open lid), and M4 and M5 MacBook Airs drive two with the lid open.
standout_why: Compared against The Office Journal under-$200 (cited), The Office Journal under-$150 (cited) and itechguides 'Xebec, Trio, and More' (cited); deskfinds under-$200 returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Office Journal under-$200 says only that base M1, M2 and M3 MacBooks 'support limited external displays natively' and that two-screen setups 'usually need two USB-C ports that carry video'. The under-$150 page has no MacBook limit at all. itechguides explains DisplayLink against native video in general and quotes Amazon listings. None gives Apple's count per chip, the M3 lid-closed condition, or the M4/M5 cutoff. Rated 2 and not 3 for two reasons: ChatGPT's own answer already carries the general M1/M2/M3 caveat, and I could not open FOPO's or Mobile Pixels' pages today (HTTP 429 on every attempt), so the maker-side cell for each of our rows is missing.
decides: The finding splits the under-$200 pick by laptop. This rests on the S1 and S7 being driver-free as our records say; I could not re-read FOPO's pages today. On an M1, M2 or M3 MacBook Air, a driver-free two-screen extender (FOPO S1, FOPO S7) can light only one added screen with the lid open, so the honest pick there is a single added screen. On an M4 or M5 MacBook Air, Apple's page allows two external displays with the lid open, so a driver-free dual is not blocked by the Mac's display count. For Windows laptops, the only rule I can source is the Office Journal's general one of two video-capable USB-C ports for two screens, not FOPO's own statement. The page should not print a per-model Mac cell for the S1 or S7 until FOPO's page is read.

findings.label: MacBook Air (M1, 2020): external displays supported alongside the built-in display
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M1, 2020) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. A driver-free dual extender needs two native display outputs, so only one of its screens can be driven.

findings.label: MacBook Air (M2, 2022): external displays supported alongside the built-in display
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'.

findings.label: MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip: conditions for two external displays
findings.value: 2 external displays only with the lid closed; needs macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later (MacBook Air) or 14.6 or later (MacBook Pro), the Mac on power, and an external keyboard and mouse or trackpad; opening the lid makes the secondary external display go dark or disconnect
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple page published 2024-07-30. Inference (mine, not Apple's): an extender that hangs on or stands behind the open lid is used with the lid open, so this mode does not help it.

findings.label: MacBook Air with M4 or M5 chip: external displays supported alongside the built-in display
findings.value: up to 2 external displays in addition to the built-in display; closing the lid does not increase the count
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple page published 2026-03-10. Quotes: 'MacBook Air models with the M4 chip support up to two external displays simultaneously in addition to the built-in display'; same sentence for M5. This is the generation where a driver-free dual extender is no longer blocked by the Mac's display count.

findings.label: What the cited rival says about ports for two added screens and about base Macs
findings.value: 'Two-screen setups usually need two USB-C ports that carry video (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt).' and 'Base M1, M2 and M3 MacBooks support limited external displays natively.' (no count per chip, no lid condition, no M4/M5)
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders Under $200: Single and Triple-Screen (2026) | The Office Journal
findings.note: Its rows: ZUMWALT P7 15.6" (about $190), an unbranded 15.6" detachable (about $110), Cevaton 15.6" detachable (about $125), an unbranded 14.2" (about $90); prices 'at the time of writing', page dated 2026-09-11.

findings.label: Video path as the rival reports the listing
findings.value: 2 USB-C cables if the laptop has two full-featured USB-C ports; M1, M2 and M3 MacBooks and laptops without such ports need an extra H5-T cable (not included) plus HDMI and USB-A connections and a driver
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders Under $200: Single and Triple-Screen (2026) | The Office Journal
findings.note: This is The Office Journal's account of ZUMWALT's listing, not the listing itself. itechguides quotes the same Amazon listing (B0G7FN2XT4): 'Connect via H5-T + HDMI + USB-A cable ( to external power, driver installation required)', https://www.itechguides.com/best-laptop-screen-extenders-in-2025-top-picks-and-buying-guide/ read 2026-11-21.

findings.label: What the second cited rival says about compatibility
findings.value: 'Single-cable use needs a USB-C port with video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt)'; otherwise HDMI plus a separate USB cable for power. No MacBook limit, no driver or DisplayLink mention, no operating-system list
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders Under $150 (2026) | The Office Journal
findings.note: Rows are single-screen extenders (Cevaton 15.6", KEFEYA 14", ROYY 14", Miesebe 14").

findings.label: What the third cited rival says about drivers
findings.value: 'A native USB-C or HDMI display should not normally require a DisplayLink driver, while a DisplayLink-based adapter does.' and 'A USB-C connector is not, by itself, a promise of display output.'
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders in 2025: Xebec, Trio, and More
findings.note: General guidance plus quoted Amazon listing bullets; no Apple per-chip display counts. Its listed prices: 14.2" extender $79.97, KEFEYA 14" $89.99, Vixtan 14" two-added-screen $170.95, ZUMWALT P7 $175.59, KYY 15.6" portable monitor $55.99, stated as accurate on 2026-11-21.
